checks.why: a test that runs bin/cli.js as a child process by its path (a path.join of literals held in a constant) covers everything the script reaches: the path is the only link, and without it the answer said no test reaches shout
the link is its own rung, counted in the tests section of the plain answer, not folded into a resolved call
a path.resolve with the path in one literal, handed to spawnSync, is the same link; the script's top-level call reaches stamp

a helper beside the tests starts the script (`const run = args => spawnSync(node, [bin].concat(args))`, bin a require.resolve with no extension): the tests that call the helper run the script, and the route is labelled as the spawn, not as a fixture
CONTROL: a test that only READS the script's file with the same path shape starts no process and runs none of it, so it gains no link
CONTROL: a module no test spawns keeps exactly the tests that call it
test-impact for an edit to a module the script reaches selects the test that spawns the script, and not the test that only reads the script's file
